stories.title: EU sustainability reporting rules narrowed
stories.summary: Directive 2026/470 narrows the scope of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive. Many companies will no longer be subject to these reporting obligations or will face them later. Additional requirements regarding products, packaging, and sustainability advertising will apply instead.

stories.title: FCA to regulate ESG ratings providers
stories.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority will impose a new regulatory regime on ESG ratings providers starting in 2028. Firms must secure authorisation from the regulator to operate. The move aims to bring more reliability to the market. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: SUSEP proposes new sustainability reporting framework
stories.summary: The Superintendence of Private Insurance has submitted a draft resolution to replace current sustainability requirements for insurance companies, pension entities, and reinsurers. The proposal includes a new guidance manual for standard tables in sustainability reports and aims to align local practices with international standards.

stories.title: Deloitte benchmarks Finnish CSRD reporting
stories.summary: Deloitte Finland’s second benchmarking report examines how 22 large and listed Finnish companies are navigating the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive. Following two years of formal reporting, companies are building on initial experience while the regulatory landscape continues to evolve and reporting practices remain in flux.

stories.title: GRI publishes new reporting guidelines draft
stories.summary: The Global Reporting Initiative has published the latest draft of its next generation of reporting guidelines, G4, for public review. The organization describes the draft as the future of corporate reporting. The document is currently open for comment.

stories.title: China issues sustainability reporting guidelines
stories.summary: China’s securities exchanges have issued guidelines requiring specific listed companies to publicly disclose sustainability reports. Covered firms include constituents of the SSE 180, STAR 50, Shenzhen 100, and ChiNext indices, as well as dual-listed companies. Reports for the 2025 calendar year are due by 30 April 2026.

stories.title: Deloitte launches AI tool to detect greenwashing
stories.summary: Deloitte has launched the Green Claims Navigator, an AI-powered tool designed to detect misleading environmental statements. The software scans a company’s content ecosystem, including websites, reports, and packaging, to identify claims that may not align with current sustainability regulations.

stories.title: Deloitte releases Green Claims Navigator
stories.summary: Deloitte has launched Green Claims Navigator to help companies detect greenwashing and ensure compliance with new regulations. The tool monitors marketing materials against rules like the EU’s Directive on Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition. Companies are increasingly expected to substantiate claims with objective evidence.

stories.title: ISSB proposes nature-related disclosure standards
stories.summary: The International Sustainability Standards Board has proposed a new practice statement for disclosing nature-related risks and opportunities. Companies applying IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards can expect greater clarity on location-specific analysis and the connections between nature and climate. The proposal is currently under discussion.

stories.title: Bangladesh carbon credit earnings lag potential
stories.summary: Bangladesh earns approximately $16 million annually from carbon credits, despite a potential capacity of $1 billion. The government has finalized a national carbon credit framework and plans to establish a registry to remove bureaucratic hurdles and attract investment for solar and other eligible projects.

stories.title: EKI Energy contests SEBI revenue ruling
stories.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India found that EKI Energy recognized Rs 197.04 crore in revenue early. The regulator argues that distributing cookstoves did not complete contract obligations while verification was pending. EKI Energy is contesting the order and the technical accounting interpretation.

stories.title: McKinsey estimates climate adaptation costs
stories.summary: McKinsey Global Institute estimates that annual climate adaptation costs could reach $1.2 trillion by 2050 under a 2°C warming scenario. The report identifies 20 measures to protect assets against heat, drought, and flooding. Currently, only a fraction of that amount is deployed.

stories.title: Verra coal retirement methodology wins quality label
stories.summary: The Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market has approved Verra’s coal plant retirement methodology, VM0052, as meeting its Core Carbon Principles. Projects can earn credits for emissions avoided when plants close early. Each project must implement a just transition plan for affected workers.

stories.title: Albania plans carbon market entry by 2035
stories.summary: Albania aims to sell carbon credits and establish an emissions trading system by 2035. The plans, announced in a recent forest market report, intend to align the country with European Union standards. The framework for these markets is currently under development.

stories.title: Verra methodology gains quality benchmark
stories.summary: Verra’s VM0052 methodology has received approval from the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market. The label allows transition credits from early coal plant retirements to carry a recognized quality benchmark. The move aims to attract investors to projects replacing coal with renewable energy.

stories.title: Gabon sells forest carbon credits to SEFE
stories.summary: Gabon has agreed to sell 6 million forest carbon credits to the German state-owned energy company SEFE. The credits are certified under the ART-TREES standard and are eligible for aviation sector offsetting. The deal marks a move to generate sovereign revenue from forest protection.

stories.title: UNCTAD to launch carbon market network
stories.summary: UNCTAD plans to launch a carbon market network at COP31. The initiative is part of a broader effort to push climate finance and trade agendas. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: COP31 begins in Antalya
stories.summary: The United Nations climate summit, COP31, is scheduled to take place from 9 to 20 November 2026 in Antalya, Türkiye. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries will gather to address global climate goals amidst ongoing geopolitical tensions and rising energy costs.

stories.title: Australia leads climate talks while exporting fossil fuels
stories.summary: Climate change minister Chris Bowen is leading negotiations at COP31 in Antalya. Australia is currently urged to move away from its nearly US$100 billion fossil fuel export industry while simultaneously pushing for a global agreement to reduce reliance on coal, gas and oil.

stories.title: IPCC gridlock ahead of COP31
stories.summary: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change suspended its mid-October meeting without approving a budget or a timeline for upcoming reports. The scientific organization, which provided the foundation for the 2015 Paris climate agreement, is currently mired in political disputes and funding shortages.

stories.title: Antalya hosts COP31 climate conference
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of delegates are gathering in Antalya for COP31, running from 9 to 20 November. The summit follows the 2023 Dubai conference, which called for a transition away from fossil fuels. Organizers hope to put climate action back on the global agenda.

stories.title: EU resists new climate financing at COP31
stories.summary: European Union negotiators intend to oppose any new climate financing commitments at the COP31 summit in Antalya. The full details regarding the EU's stance on current environmental directives and potential pitfalls for member states are available to subscribers of the publication.

stories.title: EU prioritizes implementation at COP31
stories.summary: The European Union has stated its focus for COP31 will be the implementation of existing climate commitments. The bloc has emphasized that there will be no backtracking on previous agreements regarding the transition away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: Australia and Turkey co-host COP31
stories.summary: Coal exporter Australia and coal consumer Turkey are co-hosting the COP31 summit in Antalya. The nations aim to shift the focus toward clean electricity, with a proposed target to meet 35 percent of final energy demand from electricity by 2035. The planet has two hosts.

stories.title: COP31 faces 1.5C warming threshold
stories.summary: Representatives are meeting in Antalya for COP31 from 9 to 20 November. The summit faces pressure to accelerate action as projections indicate the world will overshoot the 1.5C global warming threshold, raising questions about the long-term legacy of the Paris Agreement.

stories.title: Geopolitical mood shifts ahead of COP31
stories.summary: Government and business leaders are convening in Antalya for the COP31 climate summit. The event marks the first time a conference will face a near-certain overshoot of the 1.5C warming limit. Organizers note the geopolitical mood has been influenced by recent election results in Brazil and the US.

stories.title: Sea enzyme market enters expansion phase
stories.summary: The global sea enzyme products market is entering a phase of structural expansion, according to an IndexBox report. The industry aims to valorize seafood processing by-products to deliver clean-label functionality across food and nutraceutical applications, moving away from traditional terrestrial enzyme supply chains.

stories.title: California delays plastic packaging fees
stories.summary: California lawmakers have called for delaying certain fees under Senate Bill 54 for 2026 and 2027. While businesses seek financial relief, the law continues to mandate the extensive collection and production of packaging material data, which remains unaffected by the fee delay.

stories.title: Circular economy shouldn’t be ‘waste afterthought’ at COP31: CEI - Materials Recycling World
stories.summary: 403 Forbidden Circular economy shouldn’t be ‘waste afterthought’ at COP31: CEI Materials Recycling World The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now.

stories.title: CalRecycle updates plastic reduction baseline
stories.summary: California has updated its source reduction baseline for Senate Bill 54, which takes effect 1 January 2027. The law mandates that producers selling packaging in the state must achieve a 25 percent reduction in the weight of plastic components by 2032.

stories.summary: US sets AD/CVD rulings on Korean steel plate, OCTG and wind towers US ITA and ITC issued multiple AD/CVD rulings. stories.title: Pakistan urged to adopt national EPR framework
stories.summary: Minister of State for Climate Change Dr Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal has called for a coordinated national framework for Extended Producer Responsibility. The proposal aims to improve waste sorting and recycling infrastructure to help the country transition toward a circular economy.

stories.title: Seven issues to dominate COP31
stories.summary: Government leaders are meeting in Antalya for COP31 to address rising greenhouse gas emissions. UN officials state that despite recent progress, the world is set to cross 1.5C of global warming, propelling the planet toward dangerous climate tipping points.

stories.title: Global Water Centre launches carbon credit program
stories.summary: The Global Water Centre has launched a carbon credit program to help rural water systems access financial support. The organization claims that relying on traditional philanthropy and grants is challenging and unrealistic for scaling safe drinking water projects globally.

stories.title: Aavas Financiers ESG risk rating improves
stories.summary: Morningstar Sustainalytics has improved the ESG risk rating for Aavas Financiers to 21.4 in 2026, down from 23.9 in 2025. The rating was assigned independently based on publicly available data and company disclosures. A lower numerical score indicates a reduction in assessed ESG risk.

stories.title: NTPC ESG score reaches 64.6
stories.summary: NTPC has received an upgraded ESG score of 64.6 from SES ESG Research Private Limited. The new figure improves upon a previous rating of 64.2. The agency based the assessment on the company's own responses and data for the 2025-26 financial year.

stories.title: Google invests $160 million in Malaysian water infrastructure
stories.summary: Google is investing $160 million in a new reservoir and water treatment plant in Malaysia. The project aims to support local water supplies and future data center operations. Technology companies are facing pressure to manage the environmental impact of the water and electricity required to run artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Safaricom net income rises 35.9 percent
stories.summary: Safaricom Group reported a 35.9 percent increase in net income to Sh58.2 billion in its latest half-year results. The Kenya News Agency provided the figures. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Equity Group releases 2025 sustainability report
stories.summary: Equity Group has launched its 2025 sustainability report, claiming a Sh3.1 trillion impact on communities and businesses. The company says it has pumped record cash into these sectors. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Vardhman sets 2045 net zero target
stories.summary: Vardhman Textiles has announced a target to reach net-zero emissions by 2045. The company also plans to source 60 percent of its power from green sources by 2028. Additional goals include cutting freshwater consumption by 30 percent and reducing landfill waste by 50 percent by 2030.

stories.title: NTPC ESG score updated to 64.6
stories.summary: SES ESG Research has upgraded the ESG score for NTPC from 64.2 to 64.6. The provider is a SEBI-registered Category-II firm. The revision follows the company's direct response to the agency and the submission of updated financial and sustainability data for the 2025-26 financial year.

stories.title: Jai Balaji Group plans Rs 6000 crore investment
stories.summary: Jai Balaji Group plans to invest Rs 6000 crore in West Bengal to expand its steel and renewable energy operations. The company expects the project to create 20,000 jobs. The expansion will focus on specialized alloys for defense, aerospace and railway applications.

stories.title: India secures $400 billion in renewable energy commitments
stories.summary: India has secured $400 billion in long-term renewable energy investment commitments. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi stated that the funding will support the national target of 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. The investment covers generation, transmission, storage and manufacturing projects.
